Marissa,

Attaching our standard vendor security questionnaire (Acme-Vendor-Q-2027.pdf). A few clarifying questions up front:

- For API logs: do you capture request/response payloads or only metadata? If payloads are captured for requests that include PII, how is that data redacted or encrypted?
- For admin activity logs: what's the retention default and can it be configured per-account? Is there an audit trail showing who exported logs and when?
- For immutability: do you support write-once-read-many (WORM) on exported bundles, or is immutability enforced only via customer-controlled storage (S3 Object Lock, etc.)?

Appreciate if Aditya can respond to the above and indicate what artifacts you can provide (log schema, retention policy docs, sample export manifest).

Thanks,
Lydia

lydia.grant@acme.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: Acme security review

Hi Lydia,

Thanks for the detailed questionnaire — answered the bullets below and attached the log schema CSV and SOC snapshot.

- Payloads: We do not persist full customer request/response payloads by default. API logs capture metadata (timestamps, request ID, route, status, tokenized token counts). For customers who opt-in to more detailed logging (debug mode for troubleshooting), payload capture is possible but it's stored encrypted and marked for limited retention; we recommend using redaction hooks on the client side. We can provide a redaction guide.

- Admin activity logs: Default retention in hosted mode is 90 days; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention up to custom limits. Yes, every export action is recorded in an export audit trail (who/when/destination). We can provide a sample export manifest showing the fields recorded.

- Immutability: Redwood supports export workflows designed to be append-only and compatible with WORM storage. For hosted customers we provide signed export bundles and recommend exporting to customer-owned WORM-enabled buckets (S3 Object Lock). For Dedicated/Private deployments we can enable stricter immutability controls within the deployment; we'll detail these options in the evidence package.

Artifacts attached: redwood_audit_logs_schema.csv, SOC2-Snapshot-202706.pdf

Proposed next steps:
- I'll fill out the questionnaire and return a completed copy by Fri 16 Jul.
- If you need, let's schedule a 30-min session to walk through the export/demo (Marcus can join to show the console export flow).

Best,
Aditya Rao
Security Engineering
